newsitem.title: UK: Milupa may recall baby milk in Ireland.
newsitem.headline: Milupa may recall baby milk in Ireland.

text.p: Milupa, a unit of Dutch Nutricia NV, said on Friday it was holding talks with the Irish government on a possible withdrawal of its Milumil baby milk powder.
Dennis Segal, managing director of Milupa UK, told a news conference here: "I suspect we would do that (a withdrawal) as well."
The product, which is made in France, is produced exclusively for the British and Irish markets, said Segal.
"This product is also sold in Ireland, north and south, where volumes are relatively larger (than in Britain)," he added.
Segal said that no cases of gastroenteritis linked to the milk had been reported in Northern Ireland or the Republic of Ireland.
His comments contradicted a report from Milupa's parent company Nutricia that Milumil was not sold in any other country than Britain.
Milupa earlier said it is withdrawing Milumil from the British market following suspicion there is a link between the baby powder milk and salmonella infection.
"There is no direct incontrovertible proof that the (the cause) is Milumil. It is a statistical association, but we have to take every precaution," a spokeswoman told Reuters.
